An aromatic polyol layer mixed with formal resin fragments
A basic amino acid backbone linked systematically via peptide bonds

qe: Which specific organic molecule pairing correctly structures the bicyclic purine bases required to compile nucleic acid chains?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट कार्बनिक अणु युग्म न्यूक्लिक अम्ल श्रृंखलाओं को संकलित करने के लिए आवश्यक द्विचक्रिए प्यूरीन बेस (bicyclic purine bases) को सही ढंग से संचरित करता है?

Adenine and Guanine (एडेनीन एवं ग्वानीन)
Thymine and Cytosine alternative fragments
Melamine and Triamine resin blocks

Linear tactical polyamide chains

qe: What specific structural feature differentiates the ribose pentose sugar of RNA from the deoxyribose sugar found in DNA backbones?
qh: कौन सी विशिष्ट संरचनात्मक विशेषता आरएनए के राइबोज पेंटोज शर्करा को डीएनए बैकबोन में पाए जाने वाले डीऑक्सीराइबोज शर्करा से अलग करती है?

Ribose possesses a highly reactive hydroxyl group (-OH) at the carbon-2' position, which is missing in deoxyribose (2'-कार्बन पर -OH समूह की उपस्थिति)
Ribose lacks oxygen atoms completely within its five-membered system ring
Ribose coordinates exclusively via non-ionic ester cross-links to pack mass
e: Explanation: Ribose sugar features a reactive hydroxyl group (-OH) at its 2'-carbon position. Deoxyribose removes this atom, housing a simple hydrogen (-H) at C2', making the DNA backbone more stable.

qe: What is the formal biochemical name assigned to the pyrimidine base thymine to highlight its structural origin?
qh: थायमीन (thymine) बेस को उसके संरचनात्मक उद्गम को रेखांकित करने के लिए कौन सा औपचारिक जैव रासायनिक नाम दिया गया है?
o: 2-chlorobuta-1,3-diene variant
5-Methyluracil (5-मिथाइल्यूरेसिल)
Polyhydroxy aldehyde derivative
Quaternary ammonium halide compound

qe: Which specific chemical bond forms the linkage that attaches a heterocyclic nitrogenous base to the C1' carbon position of a pentose sugar?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट रासायनिक बंध उस लिंकेज को बनाता है जो एक विषमचक्रीय नाइट्रोजनस बेस को पेंटोज शर्करा की C1' कार्बन स्थिति से जोड़ता है?

Peptide linkage systematic covalent chain
Inter-chain Disulfide cross-link bridge system

qe: What structural unit remains after a nucleotide monomer loses its terminal esterified phosphate group?
qh: एक न्यूक्लियोटाइड मोनोमर जब अपने एस्टरीकृत फॉस्फेट समूह को खो देता है, तो कौन सी संरचनात्मक इकाई शेष बचती है?

Nucleoside (न्यूक्लिओसाइड)
An active free-radical addition polymer initiator
A cross-linked three-dimensional network panel

qe: Which dynamic physical parameter allows molecular biology technicians to evaluate the operational identity of a nucleotide versus a nucleoside component during screening?
qh: कौन सा गतिशील भौतिक पैरामीटर आणविक जीवविज्ञानी को स्क्रीनिंग के दौरान न्यूक्लियोटाइड बनाम न्यूक्लिओसाइड घटक की परिचालन पहचान का मूल्यांकन करने की अनुमति देता है?

The absolute count of linear unbranched caprolactam links
The thermal window velocity computed relative to room margins
The capacity of the system to initiate homolytic chain termination

qe: Which strong covalent bond connects successive nucleotide monomers together along a single strand of DNA or RNA?

o: N-glycosidic link bridging rings together
3'-5' phosphodiester linkage (3'-5' फॉस्फोडिएस्टर बंध)
Amide linkage systematically identical to a biological peptide bond
Sulfur disulfide cross-link bridge system anchoring paths

qe: What molecular architectural arrangement details the relative directionality of the two complementary strands inside a DNA double helix model?
qh: कौन सा आणविक संरचनात्मक विन्यास डीएनए डबल हेलिक्स मॉडल के भीतर दो पूरक धागों की सापेक्ष दिशात्मकता (relative directionality) का विवरण देता है?

They exhibit anti-parallel polarity, where one strand runs 5' to 3' and the other runs 3' to 5' (प्रति-समानांतर ध्रुवता / anti-parallel)
They are arranged as separate open-chain unlinked carbohydrate blocks
They cross-link randomly into a single infusible thermosetting net plastic
e: Explanation: The twin strands of a DNA double helix run anti-parallel to one another. One strand is oriented in the 5' to 3' direction, while its complementary counter-strand features a reverse 3' to 5' alignment.

Covalent peptide linkages identical to those in globular proteins
Quaternary ammonium halide coordinate link systems

qh: डबल-स्ट्रैंडेड डीएनए ब्लॉक के भीतर एडेनीन और थायमीन बेस के बीच पूरक युग्मन (complementary pairing) कितने हाइड्रोजन बंध बनाते हैं?

Four quaternary coordinate networks

One extensive covalent bridge
Zero net thermodynamic bonds

qe: What fundamental biological concept proposed by Francis Crick describes the unidirectional flow of genetic information inside living cells?
qh: फ्रांसिस क्रिक द्वारा प्रस्तावित कौन सी मौलिक जैविक अवधारणा जीवित कोशिकाओं के भीतर आनुवंशिक जानकारी के एकदिशीय प्रवाह (unidirectional flow) का वर्णन करती है?

The Central Dogma of molecular biology (सेंट्रल डोग्मा)
The Debye-Huckel linear ionic rule
The Kohrausch independent migration statement

o: Exactly 20 base pairs block
Approximately 200 base pairs (लगभग 200 क्षारक युग्म)
4.6 million linear sequences
3300 extensive continuous strings
e: Explanation: A standard single nucleosome structure contains a double-helical DNA strand of approximately 200 base pairs coiled around a central core histone octamer assembly.

qe: Which specific histone protein is located outside the central octamer core, acting as a structural link that anchors the DNA strand to the nucleosome assembly?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट हिस्टोन प्रोटीन केंद्रीय ऑक्टामर कोर के बाहर स्थित होता है, जो एक संरचनात्मक लिंक के रूप में कार्य करता है जो डीएनए स्ट्रैंड को न्यूक्लियोसोम असेंबली से जोड़ता है?
o: H2A core variant
H1 histone (H1 हिस्टोन)
H3 processing unit
H4 coordinate segment
e: Explanation: While H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 form the internal octamer core, the H1 histone resides externally, sealing the DNA strand as it enters and exits the nucleosome core.

qe: What structural name is assigned to the regions of chromatin that are loosely packed, light-staining, and transcriptionally active inside a eukaryotic cell nucleus?
qh: यूकैरियोटिक कोशिका नाभिक के भीतर शिथिल रूप से पैक (loosely packed), हल्के रंग के और ट्रांसक्रिप्शनल रूप से सक्रिय क्रोमैटिन के क्षेत्रों को क्या संरचनात्मक नाम दिया गया है?
o: Heterochromatin dense blocks
Euchromatin (यूक्रोमैटिन)
Nucleoid boundary networks
Tactoid linear unbranched meshes
e: Explanation: Euchromatin describes the loosely coiled regions of chromatin that stain lightly. Because the DNA is accessible to transcription factors, these domains are transcriptionally active.

qe: How do heterochromatin domains contrast fundamentally with euchromatin regions regarding packing density and gene expression states?
qh: पैकिंग घनत्व (packing density) और जीन अभिव्यक्ति राज्यों के संबंध में हेटेरोक्रोमैटिन डोमेन यूक्रोमैटिन क्षेत्रों से मौलिक रूप से कैसे भिन्न हैं?
o: Heterochromatin is loosely packed and hyper-active chemically
Heterochromatin is densely and tightly packed, stains darkly, and is transcriptionally inactive (घनी रूप से पैक तथा निष्क्रिय होना)
Heterochromatin lacks histone octamers completely inside its system
There is no operational difference; both track identical color values
e: Explanation: Heterochromatin domains contain highly condensed, tightly coiled chromatin strands that stain darkly under microscopic verification. Because the DNA is tightly packed, transcription machinery cannot access it, making these regions transcriptionally inactive.

qe: Which historic transformation experiment conducted in 1928 provided the early evidence demonstrating that genetic information could be transferred between bacterial cells?
qh: 1928 में आयोजित किस ऐतिहासिक रूपांतरण प्रयोग (transformation experiment) ने शुरुआती सबूत प्रदान किए जो यह दर्शाते हैं कि आनुवंशिक जानकारी को जीवाणु कोशिकाओं के बीच स्थानांतरित किया जा सकता है?
o: The Hershey-Chase radioactive tracking run
Griffith's Transforming Principle experiment (ग्रिफिथ का प्रयोग)
The Avery-MacLeod biochemical enzymatic analysis
The Watson-Crick double helix calibration grid
e: Explanation: Frederick Griffith's 1928 experiment with Streptococcus pneumoniae strains demonstrated that an inert, heat-killed virulent strain could pass an unknown 'transforming principle' to a live avirulent strain, transforming it into a live virulent pathogen.

qe: What specific experimental animal and bacterial pathogen model did Frederick Griffith deploy to evaluate his historic Transforming Principle?
qh: फ्रेडरिक ग्रिफिथ ने अपने ऐतिहासिक ट्रांसफॉर्मिंग सिद्धांत का मूल्यांकन करने के लिए किस विशिष्ट प्रयोग पशु और जीवाणु रोगजनक मॉडल (bacterial pathogen model) को तैनात किया था?
o: Bacteriophages inside automated cellular flasks
Mice and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteria (चूहे एवं स्ट्रेप्टोकोकस न्यूमोनी)
Drosophila flies mixed with linear intermediate resins
Tobacco plants tracked relative to soil nematodes
e: Explanation: Griffith discovered the transforming principle through a series of injections into laboratory mice using smooth (virulent) and rough (avirulent) strains of the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae.

qe: Which biological trait structurally separates the smooth (S) strain of Streptococcus pneumoniae from the rough (R) strain, making it highly virulent?
qh: कौन सा जैविक लक्षण Streptococcus pneumoniae के स्मूथ (S) स्ट्रेन को रफ (R) स्ट्रेन से संरचनात्मक रूप से अलग करता है, जिससे यह अत्यधिक विषैला (highly virulent) बन जाता है?
o: The S strain contains a unique dicarboxylic lipid core skeleton
The S strain possesses a smooth polysaccharide capsule coat that shields it from the host immune system (पॉलीसेकेराइड कैप्सूल की उपस्थिति)
The S strain is a completely unbranched linear amide chain
The S strain is highly volatile and boils away rapidly under heat
e: Explanation: The smooth (S) strain synthesizes a protective polysaccharide capsule layer. This capsule uncouples host defense systems by preventing phagocytosis, making the strain virulent. The rough (R) strain lacks this capsule and is avirulent.

qe: What happened to the laboratory mice in Griffith's experiment when they were injected with a blended mixture of live rough (R) strain and heat-killed smooth (S) strain bacteria?
qh: ग्रिफिथ के प्रयोग में प्रयोगशाला के चूहों का क्या हुआ जब उन्हें जीवित रफ (R) स्ट्रेन और हीट-किल्ड स्मूथ (S) स्ट्रेन बैक्टीरिया के मिश्रित मिश्रण के साथ इंजेक्ट किया गया था?
o: The mice survived normally with zero signs of disease propagation
The mice died of pneumonia, and live smooth (S) bacteria were recovered from their blood (चूहों की मृत्यु हो गई तथा S स्ट्रेन प्राप्त हुआ)
The mice mutated into an unbranched biodegradable polyester form
The mice entered an open-ring cyclic state that blocked receptor targets
e: Explanation: Even though neither live R bacteria nor heat-killed S bacteria could kill the mice on their own, mixing them caused the mice to contract pneumonia and die. Live, virulent S strain bacteria were isolated from their blood, proving a transformation had occurred.

qe: Which team of molecular biologists conducted precise enzymatic digestion experiments between 1933 and 1944 to identify the chemical identity of Griffith's transforming principle?
qh: 1933 और 1944 के बीच आनुवंशिक रूपांतरण सिद्धांत (transforming principle) की रासायनिक पहचान की पहचान करने के लिए किस आणविक जीवविज्ञानी टीम ने सटीक एंजाइमी पाचन प्रयोग (enzymatic digestion experiments) किए थे?
o: Watson, Crick, and Rosalind Franklin structural group
Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty (एवेरी, मैकलियोड एवं मैकार्टी)
Meselson, Stahl, and Herbert Boyer alliance
Taylor, Chargaff, and Arthur Kornberg coordination team
e: Explanation: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty fractionated heat-killed S cells and tested the transforming activity of different biomolecules, discovering that only DNA could drive the transformation.

qe: Which specific enzymatic treatment systematically destroyed the transforming activity of heat-killed S strain extracts during Avery's landmark investigation?
qh: एवेरी (Avery) की ऐतिहासिक जांच के दौरान किस विशिष्ट एंजाइमी उपचार ने हीट-किल्ड एस स्ट्रेन के अर्क की रूपांतरण गतिविधि (transforming activity) को व्यवस्थित रूप से नष्ट कर दिया?
o: Protease treatments that digest structural proteins
Deoxyribonuclease (DNase) treatments that hydrolyze DNA backbones (डीऑक्सीराइबोन्यूक्लिएज / DNase उपचार)
Ribonuclease (RNase) treatments that cleave RNA transcripts
Lipase treatments that saponify membrane lipid matrices
e: Explanation: Transformation was unaffected by treating the virulent extracts with proteases or RNases. However, introducing deoxyribonuclease (DNase) fully deactivated the transforming capacity, proving that DNA was the transforming principle.

qe: What name is assigned to the historic radioactive tracking experiment conducted in 1952 that provided the final confirmation that DNA is the genetic material?
qh: 1952 में आयोजित उस ऐतिहासिक रेडियोधर्मी ट्रैकिंग प्रयोग (radioactive tracking experiment) को क्या नाम दिया गया है जिसने अंतिम पुष्टि प्रदान की कि डीएनए ही आनुवंशिक सामग्री है?
o: The Ostwald isotope dilution verification project
The Hershey-Chase Blenders experiment (हर्षे-चेज़ का प्रयोग)
The Meilsen-Stahl density gradient calibration run
The Taylor chromosomal autoradiography blueprint
e: Explanation: Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase used radioactive isotopes to track the entry of viral components into bacteria, providing definitive proof that DNA is the genetic material.

qe: Which radioactive isotopes did Hershey and Chase deploy to selectively label the protein capsule and the core DNA genome of the T2 bacteriophage?
qh: हर्षे और चेज़ ने T2 बैक्टीरियोफेज के प्रोटीन कैप्सूल और कोर डीएनए जीनोम को चुनिंदा रूप से लेबल करने के लिए कौन से रेडियोधर्मी आइसोटोप (radioactive isotopes) तैनात किए थे?
o: 14C and 15N stable element variants
35S for the sulfur-containing protein and 32P for the phosphorus-containing DNA (35S प्रोटीन के लिए एवं 32P डीएनए के लिए)
Quaternary Nitrogen tracking markers and lithium complexes
Concentrated heavy water isotopes combined with fuming indicators
e: Explanation: Hershey and Chase capitalized on elemental compositions: proteins contain sulfur but no phosphorus, while DNA contains phosphorus but no sulfur. They selectively labeled viral proteins with 35S and viral DNA with 32P.

qe: What explicit operational task describes the functional purpose of the 'blending' step executed during the Hershey-Chase virus investigation?
qh: हर्षे-चेज़ वायरस जांच के दौरान निष्पादित 'ब्लेंडिंग' (blending) चरण के कार्यात्मक उद्देश्य का क्या स्पष्ट परिचालन कार्य वर्णन करता है?
o: To accelerate the common-ion precipitation of volatile metal halides
To agitate the mixture and mechanically separate the empty viral protein coats from the bacterial cell surfaces (वायरल कोट को जीवाणु सतह से अलग करना)
To convert the solution into an unbranched biodegradable polymer network
To lower the activation energy of the water solvent matrix
e: Explanation: Blending applies mechanical agitation to sever the attachment forces holding empty viral shells (ghosts) onto the exterior surface layer of host bacterial cells after injection has finished.

qe: Following the centifugation step of the Hershey-Chase experiment, in which structural fraction was the radioactive 32P indicator detected, and what did it prove?
qh: हर्षे-चेज़ प्रयोग के सेंट्रीफ्यूजेशन चरण के बाद, किस संरचनात्मक अंश में रेडियोधर्मी 32P संकेतक का पता चला था, और इसने क्या साबित किया?
o: It floated in the liquid supernatant fraction, proving proteins enter cells
It was discovered inside the heavy pellet fraction containing the bacterial cells, proving DNA enters the host to direct replication (पैलेट या जीवाणु कोशिकाओं के भीतर मिलना)
It evaporated completely into volatile dicarboxylic organic gas configurations
It dropped down to zero absolute value via structural charring effects
e: Explanation: Centrifugation precipitates heavy bacterial cells into a bottom pellet, leaving light viral shells suspended in the liquid supernatant. The radioactivity of 32P was discovered inside the pellet, demonstrating that viral DNA enters the host cells to direct replication, which confirms it as the genetic material.

qe: Which specific criterion is not a mandatory property required for a biomolecule to successfully function as a stable genetic material?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट मानदंड एक बायोमोलेक्यूल के लिए सफलतापूर्वक एक स्थिर आनुवंशिक सामग्री के रूप में कार्य करने के लिए आवश्यक अनिवार्य गुण नहीं है?
o: It must possess the biochemical capacity to generate its own replica
It must turn highly volatile and undergo rapid structural breakdown when exposed to heat (तापमान बढ़ने पर नष्ट होने का गुण आवश्यक नहीं है)
It must be structurally and chemically stable under changing environments
It must provide an index of slow mutations required for evolutionary changes
e: Explanation: Genetic material must be highly stable and resist rapid structural or thermal breakdown. It needs to store information reliably over long periods, making structural volatility an unfavorable property.

qe: How do DNA and RNA molecules react when grouped and compared under physical guidelines of long-term structural and chemical stability?
qh: दीर्घकालिक संरचनात्मक और रासायनिक स्थिरता के भौतिक दिशानिर्देशों के तहत समूहीकृत और तुलना करने पर डीएनए और आरएनए अणु कैसे प्रतिक्रिया करते हैं?
o: RNA functions as a far more stable repository because of its ribose ring skeleton
DNA is chemically more stable than RNA because it lacks the reactive 2'-OH group and uses stable thymine instead of uracil (डीएनए अधिक स्थिर होता है)
Both maintain identical highly unstable configurations driven by pressure
Both convert instantly into volatile open-chain carbohydrate grids when cooled
e: Explanation: DNA is structurally more stable than RNA. RNA contains a highly reactive 2'-hydroxyl group (-OH) on its ribose sugar and uses uracil instead of thymine, making it chemically reactive, prone to degradation, and less suited for long-term genetic storage.

qe: What specific operational role makes RNA a superior biochemical agent compared to DNA regarding the immediate expression of genetic traits?
qh: आनुवंशिक लक्षणों की तत्काल अभिव्यक्ति (expression) के संबंध में आरएनए को डीएनए की तुलना में कौन सी विशिष्ट परिचालन भूमिका एक बेहतर जैव रासायनिक एजेंट बनाती है?
o: RNA can cross across absolute zero metal filters smoothly
RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, whereas DNA must be transcribed into RNA first (आरएनए सीधे प्रोटीन को कोड कर सकता है)
RNA blocks the central dogma Central Dogma pathways permanently
RNA is an intensive extensive parameter that resists temperature adjustments
e: Explanation: RNA can express genetic traits directly because it can translate its code directly into a protein sequence. DNA must be transcribed into an RNA intermediate first, making it dependent on RNA for protein synthesis.

qe: What foundational concept summarizes the core storage versus transmission assignments shared between DNA and RNA across global biology?
qh: वैश्विक जीव विज्ञान में डीएनए और आरएनए के बीच साझा किए जाने वाले मुख्य भंडारण (storage) बनाम संचरण (transmission) कार्यों को कौन सा मूलभूत सिद्धांत संक्षेप में प्रस्तुत करता है?
o: RNA acts as the primary long term storage matrix entirely
DNA is chemically optimized for storage of genetic information, while RNA is optimized for the transmission of genetic data (डीएनए भंडारण के लिए तथा आरएनए संचरण के लिए है)
Both handle identical overlapping steps via common-ion pathways
Both lose their functions when cross linked via structural amides
e: Explanation: Because of its chemical stability, DNA is suited to act as the long-term repository for storing genetic information. Because RNA is flexible, responsive, and short-lived, it is better suited for transmitting genetic data and directing protein synthesis.

qe: Which molecular biology law outlines the operational behavior of DNA replication, where each newly created double helix saves one original parent strand?
qh: आणविक जीवविज्ञानी का कौन सा नियम डीएनए प्रतिकृति (DNA replication) के परिचालन व्यवहार को रेखांकित करता है, जहां प्रत्येक नव निर्मित डबल हेलिक्स एक मूल जनक धागे (parent strand) को सुरक्षित रखता है?
o: The Ostwald template law
Semi-Conservative Replication mechanism (अर्ध-संरक्षी प्रतिकृति / semi-conservative)
The Gibbs free energy alignment law
The Faraday quantitative electrochemistry rule
e: Explanation: DNA replication is semi-conservative. The two strands of the parent double helix unwind and separate; each separate single strand then serves as a template to build a new complementary strand, preserving one original strand in each daughter molecule.

qe: Which historic density gradient centrifugation experiment conducted in 1958 confirmed that DNA replication is semi-conservative inside bacteria?
qh: 1958 में आयोजित किस ऐतिहासिक घनत्व प्रवणता सेंट्रीफ्यूजेशन प्रयोग (density gradient centrifugation experiment) ने पुष्टि की कि बैक्टीरिया के भीतर डीएनए प्रतिकृति अर्ध-संरक्षी होती है?
o: The Avery-MacLeod enzymatic transformation sequence
The Meselson and Stahl experiment using heavy 15N isotope templates (मेसेल्सन एवं स्टाल का प्रयोग)
The Hershey-Chase radioactive sulfur tracking project
The Watson-Crick model construction project layout
e: Explanation: Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl cultured E. coli in a heavy nitrogen isotope (15N) medium before switching them to a light nitrogen (14N) medium. Using density-gradient centrifugation, they verified that DNA replicates in a semi-conservative manner.

qe: What specific technical compound provides the density-gradient matrix medium utilized by Meselson and Stahl to separate heavy, hybrid, and light DNA molecules?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट तकनीकी यौगिक घनत्व-प्रवणता मैट्रिक्स माध्यम (density-gradient matrix medium) प्रदान करता है जिसका उपयोग मेसेल्सन और स्टाल द्वारा भारी, हाइब्रिड और हल्के डीएनए अणुओं को अलग करने के लिए किया जाता है?
o: Anhydrous calcium chloride fuming syrup
Cesium Chloride (CsCl - सीजियम क्लोराइड)
Ethidium bromide fluorescent alignment liquid
Methylene cross-linked polyolefin solution gel
e: Explanation: Meselson and Stahl used cesium chloride (CsCl) density-gradient centrifugation. Spinning CsCl at high speeds sets up a continuous density gradient, allowing DNA molecules to float and band at the position matching their buoyant density.

qe: What precise distribution profile of heavy (15N) and light (14N) strands characterizes the hybrid DNA bands isolated after E. coli cells complete exactly one generation cycle (20 minutes)?
qh: E. coli कोशिकाओं द्वारा ठीक एक पीढ़ी चक्र (20 मिनट) पूरा करने के बाद अलग किए गए हाइब्रिड डीएनए बैंड की भारी (15N) और हल्के (14N) धागे की क्या सटीक वितरण प्रोफ़ाइल विशेषता है?
o: The strands contain pure 15N isotope weights entirely on both sides
Each hybrid double helix contains one heavy parent strand (15N) and one newly synthesized light strand (14N) (एक धागा 15N तथा दूसरा 14N होना)
The strands convert completely into a single volatile dicarboxylic form
The fragments drop down to absolute zero charge markers instantly
e: Explanation: After one generation (20 minutes) in a light 14N medium, the parent 15N-15N DNA unwinds. Each heavy strand acts as a template to build a light 14N strand, producing hybrid 15N-14N DNA molecules that form a single intermediate band.

qe: What precise multi-band ratio of hybrid (15N-14N) and light (14N-14N) DNA molecules develops when the E. coli culture reaches 40 minutes (two generation cycles) during density work?
qh: घनत्व कार्य के दौरान जब E. coli संस्कृति 40 मिनट (दो पीढ़ी चक्र) तक पहुँचती है तो हाइब्रिड (15N-14N) और हल्के (14N-14N) डीएनए अणुओं का क्या सटीक मल्टी-बैंड अनुपात विकसित होता है?
o: The entire solution shifts into a single heavy bounding lane index
Equal proportions (1:1 ratio) of hybrid DNA and completely light DNA molecules (हाइब्रिड और हल्के डीएनए का समान अनुपात)
The plot converts completely into an extensive dicarboxylic layout
The system drops to a zero baseline indicator via ring closure loops
e: Explanation: After 40 minutes (two generations), the hybrid strands separate to serve as templates alongside the newer light strands. This yields a 1:1 ratio composed of two hybrid 15N-14N DNA molecules and two light 14N-14N DNA molecules.

qe: What primary biochemical catalyst acts as the principal hero enzyme required to drive, coordinate, and elongate the DNA strands during replication?
qh: कौन सा प्राथमिक जैव रासायनिक उत्प्रेरक प्रतिकृति (replication) के दौरान डीएनए धागे को चलाने, समन्वय करने और बढ़ाने के लिए आवश्यक प्रमुख हीरो एंजाइम के रूप में कार्य करता है?
o: DNA Ligase sealing agent
DNA-dependent DNA Polymerase (डीएनए-निर्भर डीएनए पॉलीमरेज)
RNA Polymerase transcription unit
Alkaline Phosphatase removing groups
e: Explanation: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase is the primary catalytic engine of replication. It coordinates the polymerization of decadeoxynucleotides, adding them sequentially onto a template strand with high speed and fidelity.

qe: What specific dual purpose do deoxynucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) fulfill during the quantitative replication cycle of a DNA molecule?
qh: डीऑक्सीन्यूक्लियोसाइड ट्राइफॉस्फेट (dNTPs) एक डीएनए अणु के मात्रात्मक प्रतिकृति चक्र के दौरान कौन सा विशिष्ट दोहरा उद्देश्य पूरा करते हैं?
o: They act as mechanical fillers to thicken the plastic layer framework
They serve as active substrates for polymerization while providing the required activation energy via high-energy phosphate bond cleavage (सब्सट्रेट एवं ऊर्जा प्रदाता दोनों होना)
They function as chemical chain retarders that slow down replication velocity
They convert the targeted solution pool into an open chain ether network
e: Explanation: Deoxynucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs, like dATP, dGTP) serve a dual role: they act as substrates for DNA synthesis and provide metabolic energy for the polymerization reaction by cleaving their high-energy pyrophosphate bonds.

qe: What architectural term defines the specific localized sequence along a genomic DNA molecule where replication loops are initiated?
qh: कौन सा संरचनात्मक शब्द एक जीनोमिक डीएनए अणु के साथ उस विशिष्ट स्थानीयकृत अनुक्रम को परिभाषित करता है जहां प्रतिकृति लूप (replication loops) शुरू किए जाते हैं?
o: Selectable marker domain section
Origin of Replication / ori site (प्रतिकृतियन का उद्गम / ori साइट)
Multiple cloning restriction sequence
Tactoid linear unbranched layout target
e: Explanation: DNA replication cannot begin randomly. It initiates at a specific, genetically defined nucleotide sequence known as the Origin of Replication (ori).

qe: Which specialized enzyme breaks the hydrogen bonds holding anti-parallel template strands together, creating the Y-shaped replication fork profile?
qh: कौन सा विशेष एंजाइम एंटी-समानांतर टेम्पलेट धागे को एक साथ रखने वाले हाइड्रोजन बंधों को तोड़ता है, जिससे Y-आकार का प्रतिकृति चिमटा (replication fork) प्रोफ़ाइल बनता है?
o: DNA Ligase chemical sealing gum
DNA Helicase (डीएनए हेलिकेज)
Topoisomerase tension releasing unit
Single stranded binding protein system
e: Explanation: DNA helicase catalyzes the ATP-driven unwinding of the double helix. By breaking the hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs, it separates the strands, creating a Y-shaped replication fork zone.

qe: What operational hazard makes the integration of the enzyme Topoisomerase mandatory ahead of a moving replication fork axis?
qh: कौन सा परिचालन खतरा चल रहे प्रतिकृति चिमटा (replication fork) अक्ष के आगे एंजाइम टोपोआइसोमिरेज (Topoisomerase) के एकीकरण को अनिवार्य बनाता है?
o: Trace polymer molecules turn volatile and disperse inside cell channels
The tension from unwinding causes severe upstream torsional strain and supercoiling, which topoisomerase releases by introducing transient cuts (सुपरकॉइलिंग या ऐंठन तनाव को दूर करना)
The single strands naturally undergo cross linking into a thermosetting resin
The backbones lose their vital phosphate groups via spontaneous shifts
e: Explanation: As helicase unwinds the double helix, it generates torsional strain and positive supercoiling ahead of the replication fork. Topoisomerase cuts, rotates, and reseals the strands to release this tension, preventing structural blocking of the fork.

qe: Why must the enzyme Primase synthesize a short temporary RNA primer piece before DNA Polymerase can begin building a new DNA strand?
qh: डीएनए पॉलीमरेज़ एक नया डीएनए धागा बनाना शुरू करने से पहले एंजाइम प्राइमेज़ (Primase) को एक छोटा अस्थायी आरएनए प्राइमर टुकड़ा क्यों संश्लेषित करना चाहिए?
o: Because DNA polymerase requires a lipophilic cross linked network to activate
Because DNA polymerase can only elongate an existing strand and requires a free 3'-OH group to initiate synthesis (प्राइमेज़ मुक्त 3'-OH समूह प्रदान करता है)
Because the template strands convert into an open chain carbohydrate without it
Because it lowers the required concentration of deoxynucleotides to zero
e: Explanation: DNA polymerase cannot initiate DNA synthesis de novo; it can only append nucleotides onto an existing strand. Primase lays down a short complementary RNA primer sequence, providing the free 3'-hydroxyl group (3'-OH) required for DNA polymerase to bind and elongate.

qe: Since DNA polymerase can synthesize a new strand strictly in the 5' to 3' direction, how does this requirement affect synthesis along the two antiparallel template strands?
qh: चूंकि डीएनए पॉलीमरेज कड़ाई से 5' से 3' दिशा में एक नया धागा संश्लेषित कर सकता है, इसलिए यह आवश्यकता दो प्रति-समानांतर टेम्पलेट धागे के साथ संश्लेषण को कैसे प्रभावित करती है?
o: Synthesis proceeds seamlessly and continuously across both strands simultaneously
One template drives continuous synthesis (leading strand), while the other drives discontinuous synthesis in short fragments (lagging strand) (एक धागे पर सतत तथा दूसरे पर असतत होना)
Both strands undergo permanent structural degradation into volatile gas states
Keep chains locked into an unbranched polyolefin tail layout format
e: Explanation: Because the double helix is anti-parallel and DNA polymerase operates exclusively in the 5' to 3' direction, synthesis is continuous on one template strand (the leading strand). On the other template strand (running in the opposite direction), synthesis occurs discontinuously in short segments, forming the lagging strand.

qe: What structural name is assigned to the short, discontinuous segments of DNA synthesized along the lagging template strand?
qh: लैगिंग टेम्पलेट धागे (lagging template strand) के साथ संश्लेषित डीएनए के छोटे, असतत खंडों को क्या संरचनात्मक नाम दिया गया है?
o: Helical replication fork elements
Okazaki fragments (ओकाजाकी खंड)
Methylene polymer network lines
Unbranched non-ionic surfactant blocks
e: Explanation: The short, discontinuous DNA segments synthesized on the lagging strand during replication are called Okazaki fragments, named after Reiji Okazaki.

qe: Which specialized genetic enzyme acts as the molecular glue required to seal nicks between consecutive Okazaki fragments, forming a continuous strand?
qh: कौन सा विशेष आनुवंशिक एंजाइम आणविक गोंद (molecular glue) के रूप में कार्य करता है जो लगातार ओकाजाकी खंडों के बीच के अंतरालों को सील करने के लिए आवश्यक है?
o: DNA Helicase unwinding engine
DNA Ligase (डीएनए लाइगेज)
Topoisomerase alignment modifier
RNA Polymerase transcribing unit
e: Explanation: DNA ligase links discontinuous Okazaki fragments together. It catalyzes the formation of a phosphodiester bond between the 3'-OH end of one fragment and the 5'-phosphate group of the next, creating a continuous lagging strand backbone.

qe: What descriptive terminology defines the genetic segments inside double-stranded DNA that actively code for single polypeptide chains?
qh: डबल-स्ट्रैंडेड डीएनए के भीतर उन आनुवंशिक खंडों को क्या वर्णनात्मक शब्दावली परिभाषित करती है जो एकल पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखलाओं के लिए सक्रिय रूप से कोड करते हैं?
o: Intron non-coding profiles
Cistron (सिस्ट्रॉन)
Promoter interface segments
Thermosetting dynamic network sets
e: Explanation: A cistron is defined in molecular biology as a segment of DNA that encodes the structural primary sequence for a single polypeptide chain.

qe: How do monocistronic structural gene configurations look fundamentally different from polycistronic setups regarding gene layout layouts?
qh: जीन लेआउट लेआउट के संबंध में मोनोसिस्ट्रोनिक संरचनात्मक जीन विन्यास (monocistronic structural gene configurations) पॉलीसिस्ट्रोनिक延सेटअप से मौलिक रूप से कैसे भिन्न दिखते हैं?
o: Monocistronic units lack basic nitrogenous bases completely across all zones

Monocistronic genes code for a single polypeptide and are typical of eukaryotes, whereas polycistronic genes code for multiple polypeptides from one promoter in prokaryotes (मोनोसिस्ट्रोनिक एक पॉलीपेप्टाइड तथा पॉलीसिस्ट्रोनिक कई पॉलीपेप्टाइड को कोड करता है)
Monocistronic genes are composed entirely of cross-linked phenol meshes
Both are completely unbranched extensive parameters driven by pressure loops
e: Explanation: Eukaryotes generally exhibit monocistronic structural genes, where a single promoter drives the transcription of one polypeptide. Prokaryotes feature polycistronic genes organized into operons, where a single promoter drives the transcription of a single mRNA molecule encoding multiple distinct proteins.

qe: Applying the foundational mnemonic rule 'NICE', what precise structural definition separates an intron from an exon inside eukaryotic split genes?
qh: 'NICE' के मूलभूत नियम को लागू करते हुए, कौन सी सटीक संरचनात्मक परिभाषा यूकैरियोट स्प्लिट जीन के भीतर एक इंट्रॉन को एक एक्सॉन से अलग करती है?
o: Introns are highly reactive polyhydroxy aldehyde sections across chains

Introns are non-coding intervening sequences that are removed during splicing, while exons are coding sequences that appear in mature RNA transcripts (इंट्रॉन गैर-कोडिंग अनुक्रम तथा एक्सॉन कोडिंग अनुक्रम हैं)
Introns form stable three-dimensional cross-linked network lattices
Both are entirely limited to volatile open-chain carbohydrate formats
e: Explanation: Eukaryotic split genes contain alternating regions: exons are coding sequences that are preserved and expressed in mature mRNA transcripts, while introns are non-coding intervening sequences that are spliced out and removed during maturation.

qe: What terminology defines a newly synthesized, primary eukaryotic RNA transcript that still retains both coding exons and non-coding introns?
qh: कौन सी शब्दावली एक नए संश्लेषित, प्राथमिक यूकैरियोटिक आरएनए प्रतिलेख (transcript) को परिभाषित करती है जिसमें अभी भी कोडिंग एक्सॉन और गैर-कोडिंग इंट्रॉन दोनों मौजूद होते हैं?
o: Mature functional messenger RNA strand
Heterogeneous nuclear RNA / hnRNA (विषमांगी न्यूक्लीय आरएनए / hnRNA)
Unbranched non-ionic linear surfactant unit
Cross-linked network alignment factor index
e: Explanation: The raw, un-spliced primary transcript generated by RNA polymerase II in eukaryotes contains both exons and introns, designated systematically as heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).

qe: Which specific biochemical enzyme handles the transcription of the vast majority of heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA) inside eukaryotic cell nuclei?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट जैव रासायनिक एंजाइम यूकैरियोटिक कोशिका नाभिक के भीतर विषमांगी न्यूक्लीय आरएनए (hnRNA) के विशाल बहुमत के प्रतिलेखन (transcription) को संभालता है?
o: RNA Polymerase I driving ribosomal loops
RNA Polymerase II (आरएनए पॉलीमरेज II)
RNA Polymerase III producing transfer units
DNA Polymerase III executing replication steps
e: Explanation: Eukaryotic nuclei possess three distinct RNA polymerases. RNA Polymerase II transcribes the genes that encode proteins, generating the primary hnRNA transcripts that mature into mRNA.

qe: What architectural change defines the post-transcriptional processing modification known as 'capping' at the 5' end of a eukaryotic pre-mRNA transcript?
qh: कौन सा संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन यूकैरियोटिक प्री-mRNA प्रतिलेख के 5' छोर पर 'कैपिंग' (capping) के रूप में जाने जाने वाले पोस्ट-ट्रांसक्रिप्शनल प्रोसेसिंग संशोधन को परिभाषित करता है?
o: The addition of a long chain of unbranched natural cellulose molecules
The covalent addition of an unusual nucleotide, methyl guanosine triphosphate, to the 5'-terminal end (मिथाइल ग्वानोसीन ट्राइफॉस्फेट का जुड़ना)
The high-pressure insertion of short-chain volatile organic solvents
The homolytic cleavage of base pair backbones using peroxide initiators
e: Explanation: Capping protects the nascent pre-mRNA transcript from exonuclease degradation. It involves adding a modified nucleotide, 7-methylguanosine triphosphate, to the 5'-end of the hnRNA molecule.

qe: What name is assigned to the post-transcriptional processing event where non-coding introns are cleanly removed and coding exons are covalently spliced together?
qh: उस पोस्ट-ट्रांसक्रिप्शनल प्रोसेसिंग घटना को क्या नाम दिया गया है जहां गैर-कोडिंग इंट्रॉन को साफ रूप से हटा दिया जाता है और कोडिंग एक्सॉन को सहसंयोजक रूप से एक साथ जोड़ा जाता है?
o: Polyadenylation terminal tailing route
Splicing (स्प्लिसिंग / आरएनए संबंधन)
Bredig's arc mechanical dispersion step
Ziegler-Natta coordination polymerization sequence
e: Explanation: Splicing is the crucial processing step where introns are removed from the primary hnRNA transcript and exons are joined together to form a continuous coding sequence, yielding mature functional mRNA.

qe: What architectural modification details the 'tailing' step executed at the 3' end of a maturing eukaryotic mRNA molecule?
qh: कौन सा संरचनात्मक संशोधन एक परिपक्व यूकैरियोटिक mRNA अणु के 3' छोर पर निष्पादित 'टेलिंग' (tailing) चरण का विवरण देता है?
o: The addition of heavy cross-linked phenolic thermosetting net resins
The template-independent addition of approximately 200-300 adenylate residues to form a poly-A tail (पॉली-A पूंछ का निर्माण / टेलिंग)
The complete conversion of all carbon modules into uncharged volatile amides
The introduction of flexible structural polyisoprene elastomer chains
e: Explanation: Tailing provides stability and facilitates nuclear export. It involves adding a polyadenylation tail, composed of approximately 200-300 adenylate residues (poly-A tail), to the 3'-end of the processed mRNA molecule in a template-independent manner.

qe: What is the total number of distinct genetic codons that compile the universal genetic code dictionary, and how many code for active amino acids?
qh: सार्वभौमिक आनुवंशिक कोड शब्दकोश को संकलित करने वाले विशिष्ट आनुवंशिक कोडन (genetic codons) की कुल संख्या क्या है, और कितने सक्रिय अमीनो एसिड के लिए कोड करते हैं?
o: 16 total codes, where 16 code for functional units
64 total codons, where 61 code for amino acids and 3 act as stop indicators (कुल 64 कोडन जिनमें 61 अमीनो अम्ल के लिए हैं)
20 total blocks, where 20 code for dicarboxylic entries
48502 total fragments, where 5386 represent active items
e: Explanation: The triplet genetic code generates exactly 4^3 = 64 distinct codons. Among these, 61 codons specify and code for amino acids, while the remaining 3 codons function as stop indicators that terminate translation.

qe: What terminology defines the unique architectural feature of the genetic code known as 'degeneracy'?
qh: 'अपभ्रष्टता' (degeneracy) के रूप में जाने जाने वाले आनुवंशिक कोड की अनूठी संरचनात्मक विशेषता को क्या शब्दावली परिभाषित करती है?
o: A single codon can simultaneously code for multiple different amino acids
A single amino acid can be specified and coded by more than one distinct codon (एक से अधिक कोडन द्वारा एक अमीनो अम्ल का कोडिंग)
The codons turn completely volatile and drop down to zero value metrics
The genetic dictionary changes properties dynamically based on solution pressure
e: Explanation: The genetic code is redundant or degenerate. Because there are 61 amino-acid-specifying codons but only 20 standard amino acids, many amino acids are specified by more than one distinct codon (e.g., phenylalanine is targeted by both UUU and UUC).

qe: Which specific initiation codon serves the dual role of initiating translation while coding for the amino acid methionine?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट दीक्षा कोडन (initiation codon) अमीनो एसिड मेथिओनिन के लिए कोडिंग करते हुए अनुवाद शुरू करने की दोहरी भूमिका निभाता है?
o: UUU phenylalanine code
AUG codon (AUG कोडन)
UAA ochre terminator factor
UGA opel stop marker segment
e: Explanation: The triplet codon AUG plays a dual role in molecular genetics: it codes for the essential amino acid methionine and serves as the universal initiation marker that establishes the reading frame for ribosomes.

qe: Which functional pairing correctly lists the classic nonsense or 'stop' codons that terminate polypeptide chain synthesis?
qh: कौन सा कार्यात्मक युग्म क्लासिक नॉनसेंस या 'स्टॉप' कोडन (stop codons) को सही ढंग से सूचीबद्ध करता है जो पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला संश्लेषण को समाप्त करते हैं?
o: AUG, GUG, and UUU initiation entries
UAA, UAG, and UGA (UAA, UAG एवं UGA स्टॉप कोडन)
GAA, GAG, and GUG alternative blocks
CCA, CCC, and CCG structural segments
e: Explanation: Three codons do not code for any amino acid residues. Named nonsense or stop codons, the triplet arrangements UAA (ochre), UAG (amber), and UGA (opal) signal release factors to terminate translation.

qe: What name is assigned to the regions of an mRNA molecule that are situated before the start codon and after the stop codon, which are essential for translation efficiency?
qh: एक mRNA अणु के उन क्षेत्रों को क्या नाम दिया गया है जो स्टार्ट कोडन से पहले और स्टॉप कोडन के बाद स्थित होते हैं, जो अनुवाद दक्षता के लिए आवश्यक हैं?
o: Exon coding domains
Untranslated Regions / UTRs (अननुवादित क्षेत्र / UTRs)
Cistronic overlapping fields
Polyamide structural link sets
e: Explanation: Messenger RNA molecules contain sequences flanking the coding frame: located before the start codon at the 5'-end and after the stop codon at the 3'-end, these non-translated segments are designated as Untranslated Regions (UTRs) and are vital for translation efficiency.

qe: What direct physical consequence characterizes a point mutation, differentiating it from an extensive frame-shift mutation?
qh: कौन सा प्रत्यक्ष भौतिक परिणाम एक बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन (point mutation) की विशेषता है, जो इसे व्यापक फ्रेम-शिफ्ट उत्परिवर्तन से अलग करता है?
o: The entire macromolecule cross-links into an insoluble solid net layer
A change involving the substitution of a single base pair inside the DNA sequence (एकल क्षारक युग्म में परिवर्तन)
The automatic loss of all nitrogen bases across the targeted cistron
The sudden volatilization of the sugar phosphate framework profile
e: Explanation: A point mutation is a genetic change that involves the substitution of a single nucleotide base pair within a DNA sequence, as seen in sickle-cell anemia, distinct from multi-base insertions or deletions that disrupt the reading frame.

qe: What classical pathological disorder is driven by a single-base pair point mutation that switches a GAG codon into GUG along the beta-globin gene?
qh: बीटा-ग्लोबिन जीन के साथ GAG कोडन को GUG में बदलने वाले एकल-क्षारक युग्म बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन द्वारा कौन सा शास्त्रीय रोग संबंधी विकार संचालित होता है?
o: Corneal visual xerophthalmia errors
Sickle-cell Anemia (दात्र कोशिका अरक्तता / सिकल-सेल एनीमिया)
Severe Combined Immunodeficiency disease
Fragile gums scurvy leakage anomalies
e: Explanation: Sickle-cell anemia is a classic molecular disease caused by a single point mutation in the beta-globin gene, converting a GAG codon (glutamic acid) into GUG (valine). This alters hemoglobin conformation under low oxygen tension.

qe: What unique structural molecule acts as the physical adapter that carries specific amino acids to coordinate with matching codons along an mRNA template?
qh: कौन सा अनूठा संरचनात्मक अणु भौतिक एडेप्टर (adapter) के रूप में कार्य करता है जो एक mRNA टेम्पलेट के साथ मिलान कोडन के साथ समन्वय करने के लिए विशिष्ट अमीनो एसिड ले जाता है?
o: Ribosomal structural component matrix
Transfer RNA / tRNA / Adapter RNA (अंतरण आरएनए / tRNA)
Heterogeneous nuclear transcript block
Linear step-growth polyamide string segment
e: Explanation: Transfer RNA (tRNA) serves as an adapter molecule. It contains an anti-codon loop that reads and pairs with complementary codons along the mRNA template and an amino acid acceptor stem that carries the corresponding amino acid residue.

qe: What macro name is assigned to describe the two-dimensional folded layout model of a transfer RNA (tRNA) molecule?
qh: कार्यात्मक ट्रांसफर आरएनए (tRNA) अणु के द्वि-आयामी मुड़े हुए लेआउट मॉडल का वर्णन करने के लिए क्या मैक्रो नाम दिया गया है?
o: Inverted L-shape layout framework
Clover-leaf structure (क्लोवर-लीफ / तिपतिया घास की पत्ती जैसी संरचना)
Linear unbranched polysaccharide matrix sheet
Thermosetting cross-linked network model mesh
e: Explanation: In two dimensions, the secondary folding structure of a tRNA molecule folds into loops and arms resembling a clover-leaf blueprint. In three dimensions, it folds into a compact inverted L-shape configuration.

qe: What specific operational naming convention describes the structural shape of a tRNA molecule folded in three dimensions?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट परिचालन नामकरण कंवेंशन तीन आयामों में मुड़े हुए tRNA अणु के संरचनात्मक आकार का वर्णन करता है?
o: Clover-leaf secondary blueprint notation
Inverted L-shape configuration (उल्टा L-आकार)
Unbranched dicarboxylic straight alkane tail block
Quaternary ammonium halide coordination coordinate mesh
e: Explanation: X-ray crystallography shows that the three-dimensional tertiary structure of a functional tRNA molecule folds into an inverted L-shaped conformation.

qe: What specific structural arrangement of nucleotides defines the amino acid acceptor stem interface found at the 3' end of a tRNA molecule?
qh: न्यूक्लियोटाइड की कौन सी विशिष्ट संरचनात्मक व्यवस्था एक tRNA अणु के 3' छोर पर पाए जाने वाले अमीनो अम्ल स्वीकर्ता स्टेम इंटरफ़ेस (amino acid acceptor stem interface) को परिभाषित करती है?
o: An unbranched non-ionic polyolefin sequence
CCA-hydroxy terminal sequence (CCA सिरा)
AUG initiation codon cluster matrix
UAA opel stop indicator sequence segment
e: Explanation: The amino acid acceptor stem at the 3'-terminal end of every functional tRNA molecule features a conserved single-stranded sequence: 5'-CCA-3', where the hydroxyl group binds covalently to its specific amino acid residue.

qe: In a standard DNA strand, what specific chemical linkage connects the nucleotide monomers to form a polynucleotide chain?
qh: एक मानक डीएनए धागे (DNA strand) में, पॉलिन्यूक्लियोटाइड श्रृंखला बनाने के लिए न्यूक्लियोटाइड मोनोमर्स को कौन सा विशिष्ट रासायनिक बंधन (chemical linkage) जोड़ता है?
o: N-glycosidic bonds
3'-5' Phosphodiester bonds (3'-5' फॉस्फोडिएस्टर बंध)
Peptide bonds
Hydrogen bonds
e: Explanation: Nucleotides are linked together in a DNA strand by 3'-5' phosphodiester bonds, which form between the 3'-hydroxyl group of one sugar and the 5'-phosphate group of the adjacent nucleotide.

qe: What structural component is missing in a nucleoside that defines its primary difference from a nucleotide?
qh: न्यूक्लियोसाइड (nucleoside) में कौन सा संरचनात्मक घटक अनुपस्थित होता है जो इसे न्यूक्लियोटाइड से अलग बनाता है?
o: Nitrogenous base
Pentose sugar
Phosphate group (फॉस्फेट समूह)
Hydroxyl group
e: Explanation: A nucleoside consists only of a nitrogenous base and a pentose sugar linked by an N-glycosidic bond. A nucleotide is formed when a phosphate group is esterified to the 5'-OH of the nucleoside.

qe: To which chemical class of sugars do both deoxyribose and ribose belong, characterized by having five carbon atoms?
qh: डीऑक्सीराइबोज़ और राइबोज़ दोनों शर्कराओं के किस रासायनिक वर्ग (chemical class) से संबंधित हैं, जिसमें पाँच कार्बन परमाणु होते हैं?
o: Trioses
Hexoses
Pentoses (पेंटोज़)
Polysaccharides
e: Explanation: Both ribose (in RNA) and deoxyribose (in DNA) are five-carbon sugars, placing them in the pentose sugar category.

qe: What physical structural characteristic of the DNA double helix is maintained by the specific pairing of purines with pyrimidines?
qh: डीएनए डबल हेलिक्स की कौन सी भौतिक संरचनात्मक विशेषता प्यूरीन और पिरिमिडीन के विशिष्ट युग्मन (pairing) द्वारा बनाए रखी जाती है?
o: The antiparallel nature of the two strands
Uniform width throughout the DNA helix (डीएनए की एकसमान चौड़ाई)
The semi-conservative mode of replication
Uniform length across all distinct DNA types
e: Explanation: Pairing a bulky purine with a smaller pyrimidine ensures that the distance between the two strands remains constant (approx. 20 Å), resulting in a uniform width across the entire length of the DNA helix.

qe: How do the net electric charges of DNA and histones differ when they associate to form nucleosomes?
qh: जब न्यूक्लियोसोम बनाने के लिए डीएनए और हिस्टोन जुड़ते हैं, तो उनके शुद्ध विद्युत आवेश (net electric charges) कैसे भिन्न होते हैं?
o: Both carry a net positive charge
Both carry a net negative charge
DNA is negative, and Histones are positive (डीएनए ऋणात्मक एवं हिस्टोन धनात्मक)
Both carry zero net charge
e: Explanation: DNA is negatively charged due to its phosphate backbone. Histones are rich in basic amino acids like lysine and arginine, which carry a net positive charge at physiological pH, allowing for tight electrostatic association.

qe: In the transcription unit, where are the promoter and terminator sites located relative to the coding strand?
qh: ट्रांसक्रिप्शन यूनिट में, कोडिंग धागे के सापेक्ष प्रमोटर (promoter) और टर्मिनेटर (terminator) साइटें कहाँ स्थित होती हैं?
o: Both are located at the 3' (downstream) end
Promoter is at the 5' (upstream) end, and Terminator is at the 3' (downstream) end (प्रमोटर 5' पर एवं टर्मिनेटर 3' पर)
Only the 5' end for both sites
Only the 3' end for both sites
e: Explanation: In a transcription unit, the promoter serves as the RNA polymerase binding site and is located at the 5' end (upstream) of the structural gene. The terminator defines the end of transcription and is located at the 3' end (downstream).

qe: Why is sickle-cell anaemia accurately classified as a 'molecular disease'?
qh: सिकल-सेल एनीमिया (sickle-cell anaemia) को 'आणविक रोग' (molecular disease) के रूप में सटीक रूप से क्यों वर्गीकृत किया गया है?
o: Because it can be easily treated with high-dose iron supplements
Because it is caused by a specific point mutation in the beta-globin chain gene (बीटा-ग्लोबिन जीन में बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन)
Because it grants complete immunity to malaria infections
Because it is caused by viral capsid structural folding
e: Explanation: Sickle-cell anaemia is a genetic disorder caused by a single point mutation where the amino acid glutamate is replaced by valine at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain, making it a classic molecular disease.

qe: What functional properties define the relationship of the AUG codon in protein synthesis?
qh: प्रोटीन संश्लेषण में AUG कोडन (AUG codon) के संबंध में कौन से कार्यात्मक गुण सत्य हैं?
o: It codes for methionine, and it functions as an initiation codon (मिथियोनिन के लिए कोड करना एवं दीक्षा कोडन होना)
It codes for valine only
It is an exclusively stop codon for both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
It is ignored by ribosomes during the translation phase
e: Explanation: AUG is a dual-function codon: it specifies the amino acid methionine and serves as the universal initiation signal for protein synthesis in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

qe: What scientific evidence suggests that RNA was the first genetic material on Earth?
qh: कौन सा वैज्ञानिक साक्ष्य यह बताता है कि पृथ्वी पर आरएनए (RNA) पहली आनुवंशिक सामग्री थी?
o: Proteins evolved from RNA, but RNA lacks stability
Essential life processes, such as metabolism and translation, evolved around RNA, which acts as a catalyst (मेटाबोलिज्म एवं ट्रांसलेशन आरएनए के चारों ओर विकसित हुए)
DNA was formed from RNA via spontaneous mineral precipitation
RNA molecules consist of triple-stranded lattice configurations
e: Explanation: Current research suggests life processes like translation and metabolism evolved around RNA. RNA acts as both genetic material and a catalyst, though its reactivity makes it less stable than DNA.

qe: In eukaryotic mRNA maturation, which sequences remain in the final transcript?
qh: यूकैरियोटिक mRNA परिपक्वता (maturation) में, कौन से अनुक्रम अंतिम प्रतिलेख में बने रहते हैं?
o: Introns only
Exons only (केवल एक्सॉन)
Both introns and exons
Neither introns nor exons
e: Explanation: Eukaryotic genes are 'split', meaning they contain non-coding introns and coding exons. During processing, introns are removed (spliced out), and only the exons appear in the mature, processed mRNA.

qe: Which human chromosome possesses the highest count of functional genes, and which one contains the fewest?
qh: मानव गुणसूत्रों में से किसमें कार्यात्मक जीनों की संख्या सबसे अधिक और किसमें सबसे कम है?
o: Chromosome 1 (highest) and Y (lowest) (गुणसूत्र 1 सर्वाधिक, गुणसूत्र Y न्यूनतम)
Chromosome 11 (highest) and X (lowest)
Chromosome 21 (highest) and 1 (lowest)
Chromosome X (highest) and Y (lowest)
e: Explanation: Human Genome Project data revealed that Chromosome 1 harbors the highest number of genes (approx. 2968), whereas the Y chromosome has the fewest (approx. 231 genes).

qe: Which scientists utilized X-ray diffraction data to propose the double-helix DNA model in 1953?
qh: 1953 में डीएनए डबल हेलिक्स मॉडल प्रस्तावित करने के लिए किस वैज्ञानिक जोड़ी ने एक्स-रे विवर्तन डेटा (X-ray diffraction data) का उपयोग किया था?
o: Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins
James Watson and Francis Crick (वाटसन एवं क्रिक)
Erwin Chargaff and Arthur Kornberg
Meselson and Stahl
e: Explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the famous double helix model in 1953, utilizing X-ray diffraction data generated by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin.

qe: Why must the 3'-OH group be removed or replaced when synthesizing artificial DNA strands to prevent uncontrolled polymerization?
qh: कृत्रिम डीएनए धागों को संश्लेषित करते समय अनियंत्रित पॉलीमराइजेशन को रोकने के लिए 3'-OH समूह को क्यों हटाया या प्रतिस्थापित किया जाना चाहिए?
o: Because purines interfere with pyrimidines at the 3' end
Because DNA polymerase requires a free 3'-OH group to add new nucleotides; blocking it stops chain extension (3'-OH की अनुपस्थिति से पॉलीमराइजेशन रुक जाता है)
Because the phosphate group naturally blocks the 3' position
Because 2'-OH groups initiate explosive cleavage
e: Explanation: DNA polymerase synthesizes DNA by adding nucleotides to the free 3'-OH group of the growing strand. If the 3'-OH group is blocked or absent, the polymerase cannot add the next nucleotide, effectively stopping the polymerization reaction.

qe: Why does the synthesis of the DNA lagging strand proceed in a discontinuous fashion (Okazaki fragments)?
qh: डीएनए लैगिंग स्ट्रैंड (lagging strand) का संश्लेषण असतत तरीके (ओकाजाकी खंड) से क्यों होता है?
o: Because DNA molecules are too long to synthesize continuously
Because DNA polymerase can only catalyze polymerization in one direction (5' to 3') (DNA पॉलीमरेज की एकदिशीय प्रकृति)
Because the process is fundamentally inefficient in bacteria
Because DNA ligase needs to exert a mechanical force on the strands
e: Explanation: DNA polymerase only catalyzes synthesis in the 5' to 3' direction. Since the two parent strands are anti-parallel, one strand (leading) is synthesized continuously, while the other (lagging) must be synthesized in short, discontinuous segments known as Okazaki fragments.

qe: Which specific enzyme is responsible for the transcription process in prokaryotes?
qh: प्रोकेरियोट्स में ट्रांसक्रिप्शन (transcription) प्रक्रिया के लिए कौन सा विशिष्ट एंजाइम जिम्मेदार है?
o: DNA Ligase
DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (डीएनए-निर्भर आरएनए पॉलीमरेज)
Restriction endonuclease
Taq Polymerase
e: Explanation: In prokaryotes, a single type of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is responsible for the transcription of all types of RNA (mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA).

qe: At what functional level does the regulation of gene expression primarily occur in eukaryotic systems?
qh: यूकैरियोटिक प्रणालियों में जीन अभिव्यक्ति (gene expression) का विनियमन प्राथमिक रूप से किस कार्यात्मक स्तर पर होता है?
o: During DNA replication
Transcriptional level, during the formation of primary transcripts (ट्रांसक्रिप्शनल स्तर पर)
During protein folding in the Golgi apparatus
None of these
e: Explanation: Gene expression in eukaryotes can be regulated at several levels, including transcriptional (primary transcript formation), processing (splicing), transport of mRNA, and translational levels.

qe: Regulatory proteins control transcription by interacting with RNA polymerase. What are the two primary operational modes of these proteins?
qh: नियामक प्रोटीन (regulatory proteins) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज़ के साथ बातचीत करके ट्रांसक्रिप्शन को नियंत्रित करते हैं। इन प्रोटीनों के दो प्राथमिक परिचालन मोड क्या हैं?
o: They only increase the expression rate
They only decrease the expression rate
They act as both activators and repressors (सक्रियकर्ता एवं दमनकारी दोनों के रूप में)
They bind to RNA but remain inert
e: Explanation: Regulatory proteins are transcription factors that can either promote (activators) or inhibit (repressors) the binding of RNA polymerase to the DNA promoter region, thereby regulating gene expression.

qe: Which chromosome was the last to be sequenced in the Human Genome Project (HGP)?
qh: मानव जीनोम प्रोजेक्ट (HGP) में अनुक्रमित (sequenced) होने वाला अंतिम मानव गुणसूत्र कौन सा था?
o: Chromosome 1 (गुणसूत्र 1)
Chromosome 11
Chromosome 21
Chromosome X
e: Explanation: The Human Genome Project was mostly completed in 2003, but the sequence of Chromosome 1, which is the largest human chromosome, was only completed in May 2006.

qe: What are the three major classes of RNAs involved in gene expression and protein synthesis?
qh: जीन अभिव्यक्ति और प्रोटीन संश्लेषण में शामिल आरएनए (RNA) के तीन प्रमुख वर्ग कौन से हैं?
o: mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA (mRNA, tRNA एवं rRNA)
DNA, cDNA, and mRNA
Protease, Ligase, and Polymerase
Codon, Anticodon, and Intron
e: Explanation: The three major classes of RNA required for protein synthesis are messenger RNA (mRNA) which carries the code, transfer RNA (tRNA) which transports amino acids, and ribosomal RNA (rRNA) which forms the structural components of the ribosome.

qe: What conclusion is drawn when an organism's DNA analysis shows that the ratio of A+G to T+C is not equal to one?
qh: जब किसी जीव के डीएनए विश्लेषण से पता चलता है कि A+G और T+C का अनुपात एक के बराबर नहीं है, तो क्या निष्कर्ष निकाला जाता है?
o: It is a typical double-stranded DNA
It is a single-stranded DNA molecule (यह एकल-रज्जुकी डीएनए है)
It is a double-stranded linear chromosome
No conclusion can be drawn
e: Explanation: Chargaff’s rule dictates that in double-stranded DNA, the ratio of purines (A+G) to pyrimidines (T+C) must equal 1. If this ratio is not 1, the DNA cannot be double-stranded.

qe: What is the primary factor that causes the rising of bread or idli dough during the fermentation process?
qh: किण्वन (fermentation) प्रक्रिया के दौरान ब्रेड या इडली के आटे के फूलने (rising of dough) का प्राथमिक कारण क्या है?
o: Multiplication of yeast cells only
Production of CO2 gas (CO2 गैस का उत्पादन)
Emulsification of starch proteins
Hydrolysis of wheat flour starch into sugars
e: Explanation: Baker's yeast (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*) performs fermentation on kneaded dough, releasing carbon dioxide (CO2) gas, which gets trapped, puffs up the dough, and makes it soft and spongy.

qe: Which class of enzymes can cut DNA at specific positions within the molecule?
qh: एंजाइमों का कौन सा वर्ग डीएनए को अणु के भीतर विशिष्ट स्थानों पर काट सकता है?
o: Endonuclease (एंडोन्यूक्लिएज)
Exonuclease
DNA Ligase
RNA Polymerase
e: Explanation: Endonucleases are a class of restriction enzymes that make cuts at specific internal positions within the DNA sequence.

qe: What process involves the transfer of genetic material from one bacterium to another via a virus vector?
qh: कौन सी प्रक्रिया में एक वायरस वेक्टर के माध्यम से एक जीवाणु से दूसरे जीवाणु में आनुवंशिक सामग्री का स्थानांतरण शामिल है?
o: Transduction (ट्रांसडक्शन / पारगमन)
Conjugation
Transformation
Translation
e: Explanation: Transduction is the transfer of DNA from one bacterium to another by a bacteriophage (virus). Conjugation involves cell-to-cell contact, and transformation is the uptake of naked DNA from the environment.

qe: What dye is used to visualize DNA bands after gel electrophoresis?
qh: जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस के बाद डीएनए बैंड को देखने के लिए किस डाई (dye) का उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Methylene blue
Ethidium bromide (इथिडियम ब्रोमाइड)
Bromophenol blue
Crystal violet
e: Explanation: Ethidium bromide is the standard staining agent used to visualize DNA bands after agarose gel electrophoresis; the bands fluoresce under UV light.

qe: What does the term 'restriction' signify in the name 'restriction endonuclease'?
qh: 'रिस्ट्रिक्शन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज' (restriction endonuclease) नाम में 'रिस्ट्रिक्शन' शब्द क्या दर्शाता है?
o: It cleaves phosphodiester bonds generally
It restricts the propagation of foreign DNA (bacteriophage) in the host bacterium (विदेशी डीएनए के गुणन को सीमित करना)
It prevents the bacterial cell from dividing
It binds to all cell membranes to stop growth
e: Explanation: The term 'restriction' refers to the enzyme's role in restricting or preventing the survival of foreign viral DNA (bacteriophage) within the host bacterium by cutting it at specific sequences.

qe: Which of the following is NOT required for preparing recombinant DNA molecules?
qh: पुनः संयोजक डीएनए अणु (recombinant DNA molecules) तैयार करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किसकी आवश्यकता नहीं होती है?
o: Restriction endonucleases
DNA ligase
DNA fragments
E. coli (for initial ligation) (प्रारंभिक लिगेशन के लिए E. coli की आवश्यकता नहीं)
e: Explanation: Recombinant DNA molecules are constructed *in vitro* using DNA fragments, restriction enzymes, and DNA ligase. While *E. coli* is used later for transformation, it is not required for the construction step itself.

qe: In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA molecules migrate based on their size; which move the furthest?
qh: एगारोज़ जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस में, डीएनए अणु अपने आकार के आधार पर पलायन करते हैं; कौन सा सबसे दूर जाता है?
o: The largest molecules
The smallest molecules (सबसे छोटे अणु)
Molecules with no charge
Neutral RNA fragments
e: Explanation: Because of the sieving effect of the agarose gel, smaller DNA fragments migrate through the pores more rapidly and thus travel farther than larger fragments.

qe: Which feature is the most critical for a plasmid to function successfully as a cloning vector?
qh: एक क्लोनिंग वेक्टर के रूप में सफलतापूर्वक कार्य करने के लिए प्लाज्मिड में कौन सी विशेषता सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है?
o: Origin of replication (ori) (प्रतिकृतियन का उद्गम)
High molecular weight
Presence of specific lipids
Ability to oxidize glucose
e: Explanation: The origin of replication (ori) is the most critical feature because it initiates replication. Any DNA fragment linked to this sequence can replicate within host cells, and it also regulates the copy number.

qe: During DNA isolation from bacteria, which enzyme should NOT be used to avoid degradation of the target DNA?
qh: बैक्टीरिया से डीएनए अलग करते समय, लक्षित डीएनए (target DNA) को खराब होने से बचाने के लिए किस एंजाइम का उपयोग नहीं करना चाहिए?
o: Lysozyme
Ribonuclease
Deoxyribonuclease (DNase) (डीऑक्सीराइबोन्यूक्लिएज)
Protease
e: Explanation: Deoxyribonuclease (DNase) must be avoided because it actively hydrolyzes and degrades the DNA molecule, which is the very target one is trying to isolate.

qe: What enzyme is essential for the amplification of specific DNA sequences in a PCR reaction?
qh: पीसीआर (PCR) प्रतिक्रिया में विशिष्ट डीएनए अनुक्रमों के प्रवर्धन (amplification) के लिए कौन सा एंजाइम आवश्यक है?
o: Thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) (थर्मोस्टेबल डीएनए पॉलीमरेज)
RNA polymerase
DNA ligase
Reverse transcriptase
e: Explanation: PCR amplification requires a heat-stable DNA polymerase, such as Taq polymerase (from *Thermus aquaticus*), to survive the repeated high-temperature denaturation cycles.

qe: What is the role of an antibiotic resistance gene in a vector?
qh: वेक्टर में एंटीबायोटिक प्रतिरोध जीन (antibiotic resistance gene) की क्या भूमिका है?
o: It initiates replication
It helps in the selection of transformed cells (रूपांतरित कोशिकाओं के चयन में सहायक)
It cuts the DNA at specific sites
It joins the DNA fragments
e: Explanation: Selectable markers like antibiotic resistance genes are used to identify and select transformed bacterial cells. Cells containing the vector survive in the presence of the antibiotic, while non-transformed cells die.

qe: Why is CaCl2 added to bacterial cells during transformation experiments?
qh: रूपांतरण प्रयोगों के दौरान जीवाणु कोशिकाओं में CaCl2 क्यों मिलाया जाता है?
o: To kill the bacteria
To increase the pore size in cell wall for DNA uptake (कोशिका भित्ति की पारगम्यता बढ़ाना)
To act as a source of energy
To activate the DNA ligase
e: Explanation: Divalent cations like Ca2+ (from CaCl2) increase the efficiency of DNA uptake by creating transient pores in the bacterial cell wall, making the cells 'competent'.

qe: What is the function of DNA ligase?
qh: डीएनए लाइगेज (DNA ligase) का कार्य क्या है?
o: Breaking phosphodiester bonds
Joining DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds (डीएनए टुकड़ों को जोड़ना)
Unwinding the DNA
Synthesizing RNA
e: Explanation: DNA ligase acts as a molecular glue. It facilitates the joining of DNA fragments by catalyzing the formation of phosphodiester bonds between the 3'-OH and 5'-phosphate ends.

qe: Which of these is NOT a source of restriction enzymes?
qh: इनमें से कौन प्रतिबंध एंजाइम (restriction enzymes) का स्रोत नहीं है?
o: Haemophilus influenzae
Escherichia coli
Agrobacterium tumefaciens (एग्रोबैक्टीरियम ट्यूमेफेशियंस)
Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
e: Explanation: *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* is a plant pathogen used as a cloning vector (Ti-plasmid), not as a source of restriction endonucleases, unlike the others listed.

qe: Which step in PCR is catalyzed by Taq polymerase?
qh: पीसीआर में कौन सा चरण टैक पॉलीमरेज़ (Taq polymerase) द्वारा उत्प्रेरित होता है?
o: Denaturation
Annealing
Extension (विस्तार / एक्सटेंशन)
None of these
e: Explanation: The extension step, where nucleotides are added to the primers to synthesize new DNA strands, is catalyzed by the thermostable Taq polymerase.

qe: Why might a human gene cloned in bacteria fail to produce the desired protein?
qh: बैक्टीरिया में क्लोन किया गया मानव जीन वांछित प्रोटीन का उत्पादन करने में विफल क्यों हो सकता है?
o: Bacteria lack RNA-splicing machinery for eukaryotic introns (बैक्टीरिया में स्प्लिसिंग तंत्र का अभाव)
The codons are fundamentally different
The protein is too small
Bacteria cannot grow at 37°C
e: Explanation: Eukaryotic genes contain introns (non-coding sequences). Bacteria lack the spliceosome machinery required to remove these introns from the pre-mRNA transcript, so the translated protein is often non-functional or not produced.

qe: What system yields higher protein production of a recombinant gene?
qh: कौन सी प्रणाली पुनः संयोजक जीन (recombinant gene) का उच्च प्रोटीन उत्पादन देती है?
o: Batch culture
Continuous culture system (निरंतर संवर्धन प्रणाली)
Small laboratory flask
None of these
e: Explanation: A continuous culture system allows the cells to stay in the log/exponential growth phase by constantly adding fresh medium and removing waste, leading to a much higher biomass and protein yield.

qe: Who discovered the PCR technique and won a Nobel Prize?
qh: पीसीआर तकनीक की खोज किसने की और नोबेल पुरस्कार जीता?
o: Herbert Boyer
Kary Mullis (कैरी मुलिस)
Arthur Kornberg
Hargovind Khurana
e: Explanation: Kary Mullis developed the PCR technique in 1985 and was awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 1993 for this invention.

qe: Which of the following is true about restriction enzymes?
qh: रिस्ट्रिक्शन एंजाइम के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से क्या सत्य है?
o: They are found in viruses
They recognize palindromic nucleotide sequences (पैलिंड्रोमिक अनुक्रमों को पहचानना)
They are endonucleases
Both (b) and (c)
e: Explanation: Restriction enzymes are indeed endonucleases that recognize specific palindromic DNA sequences to make precise cuts. They are found in bacteria, not viruses.

qe: What is the purpose of gel electrophoresis?
qh: जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस का उद्देश्य क्या है?
o: Amplifying DNA
Separating DNA fragments (डीएनए टुकड़ों को अलग करना)
Cutting DNA
Joining DNA
e: Explanation: Gel electrophoresis is a laboratory technique used to separate a mixture of DNA fragments based on their size (molecular weight) as they move through a gel matrix in an electric field.

qe: What specific terminology defines a DNA strand synthesized inside specific retroviruses using a viral RNA molecule as a template blueprint?
qh: कुछ वायरसों में आरएनए (RNA) को टेम्पलेट मानकर डीएनए का संश्लेषण किया जाता है, इस प्रकार बने डीएनए को क्या कहा जाता है?
o: A-DNA configuration
B-DNA helical matrix
Complementary DNA / cDNA (पूरक डीएनए / cDNA)
Recombinant rDNA strand
e: Explanation: Retroviruses like HIV carry a single-stranded RNA genome. They utilize the enzyme reverse transcriptase to polymerize an anti-parallel complementary DNA (cDNA) strand directly from the liquid RNA template.

qe: If Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl's density gradient calibration run is sustained for exactly four generation cycles inside bacteria, what is the predictable ratio of $^{15}\text{N}/^{15}\text{N} : ^{15}\text{N}/^{14}\text{N} : ^{14}\text{N}/^{14}\text{N}$ DNA configurations?
qh: यदि मेसेल्सन और स्टाल के प्रयोग को बैक्टीरिया में चार पीढ़ियों (four generations) तक जारी रखा जाए, तो चौथी पीढ़ी में विभिन्न डीएनए घनत्वों का अनुपात क्या होगा?
o: 1:1:0 heavy ratio layout
1:4:0 balanced hybrid shift
0:1:3 mixed gradient lane
0:1:7 ratio array (0:1:7 का अनुपात)
e: Explanation: The parent generation starts as pure $^{15}\text{N}$-$^{15}\text{N}$. Generation 1 yields 100% hybrid $^{15}\text{N}$-$^{14}\text{N}$. Generation 2 yields a 1:1 mix of hybrid and light ($^{14}\text{N}$-$^{14}\text{N}$) molecules. Generation 3 shifts to a 1:3 ratio. By generation 4 (80 minutes), the distribution becomes 12.5% hybrid and 87.5% light molecules, establishing a precise 0:1:7 ratio.

qe: If a geneticist maps a transcription unit whose coding strand sequence reads $5'\text{-ATGAATG-}3'$, what is the exact base arrangement along the resulting mRNA transcript?
qh: यदि एक ट्रांसक्रिप्शन यूनिट में डीएनए के कोडिंग धागे का अनुक्रम $5'\text{-ATGAATG-}3'$ है, तो इसके आरएनए प्रतिलेख (mRNA) का अनुक्रम क्या होगा?
o: 5'-AUGAAUG-3' (5'-AUGAAUG-3' अनुक्रम)
5'-UACUUAC-3'
5'-CAUUCAU-3'
5'-GUAAGUA-3$
e: Explanation: The sequence of an mRNA transcript matches the sequence of the DNA coding strand exactly in a 5' to 3' direction, with the sole chemical substitution of uracil (U) in place of thymine (T).

qe: Which specific architectural segments of a prokaryotic transcription unit are actively transcribed by the bacterial RNA polymerase holoenzyme?
qh: प्रोकैरियोट्स में आरएनए पॉलीमरेज होलोएंजाइम (RNA polymerase holoenzyme) मुख्य रूप से डीएनए के किन क्षेत्रों का प्रतिलेखन करता है?
o: The isolated upstream promoter segment exclusively
The promoter site combined directly with terminal vents
The structural gene and the terminator regions (संरचनात्मक जीन एवं टर्मिनेटर क्षेत्र)
The isolated structural gene sequences only
e: Explanation: The RNA polymerase holoenzyme binds to the promoter to initiate transcription. It then moves downstream, transcribing the structural gene sequence into mRNA until it hits the terminator region, where the nascent RNA transcript dissociates.

qe: If a messenger RNA triplet codon sequence displays the code $5'\text{-AUG-}3'$, what is the complementary anti-codon arrangement required on the pairing tRNA adapter molecule?
qh: यदि mRNA में एक कोडन का अनुक्रम $5'\text{-AUG-}3'$ है, तो इसके साथ युग्मन करने वाले ट्रांसफर आरएनए (tRNA) का अनुक्रम क्या होना चाहिए?
o: 5'-UAC-3' (5'-UAC-3' अनुक्रम)
e: Explanation: Anti-parallel base-pairing rules dictate that a $5'\text{-AUG-}3'$ mRNA codon pairs with a complementary tRNA anti-codon. Reading in the standard 5' to 3' direction, this anti-codon matches the sequence 5'-UAC-3' (or 3'-CAU-5').

qe: At which specific coordinate terminus of a transfer RNA (tRNA) molecule does an activated amino acid residue bind covalently?
qh: एक एमाइनो अम्ल (amino acid) ट्रांसफर आरएनए (tRNA) अणु के किस विशिष्ट सिरे पर आकर जुड़ता है?
o: The 5'-phosphate terminal end
The 3'-hydroxyl terminal end containing the CCA-OH sequence (3'-सिरा / CCA सिरा)
The loop centered around the anticodon base pair slot
The highly reactive internal dihydroxyuridine loop
e: Explanation: The amino acid acceptor stem is located at the 3'-terminal end of a tRNA molecule. It features a conserved single-stranded 5'-CCA-3' sequence that forms a covalent ester bond with the amino acid via its terminal hydroxyl group ($-OH$).

qe: What localized structural milestone triggers the initialization of protein translation when an mRNA transcript enters the cellular cytoplasm?
qh: अनुवाद (translation) की प्रक्रिया शुरू करने के लिए, मैसेंजर आरएनए (mRNA) सबसे पहले राइबोसोम के किस भाग से जुड़ता है?
o: The mRNA binds to the smaller ribosomal sub-unit configuration (छोटे राइबोसोमल सब-यूनिट से)
The transcript slots directly into the heavy matrix of the larger ribosomal sub-unit
The molecule wraps randomly around the complete intact assembled ribosome
The sequence targets non-conducting quaternary nitrogen lines
e: Explanation: In its resting or inactive state, a ribosome exists as separate large and small subunits. Translation begins when the smaller ribosomal subunit encounters and binds to the mRNA transcript near its 5' end.

qe: Under what clear molecular guidelines does the polycistronic lac operon system inside *E. coli* switch into an active 'ON' state?
qh: *E. coli* जीवाणु में, लैक ओपेरॉन (lac operon) तंत्र किस विशिष्ट परिस्थिति में सक्रिय या चालू (switched ON) होता है?
o: Lactose is present and binds directly to the repressor protein, deactivating it (लैक्टोज की उपस्थिति में दमनकारी का निष्क्रिय होना)
The regulatory repressor protein locks tightly onto the operator domain
RNA polymerase anchors to an isolated uncharged operator slot
Lactose molecules condense with the structural alpha-helix channels
e: Explanation: The lac operon turns on when lactose is present to act as an inducer. Lactose binds to the active repressor protein, causing a structural change that deactivates it. This prevents the repressor from binding to the operator, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe the operon.

qe: What are the two primary physical tasks handled by basic histone octamers when packing macro DNA molecules inside eukaryotic nuclei?
qh: यूकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में डीएनए पैकेजिंग के दौरान मुख्य हिस्टोन ऑक्टामर (histone octamer) कौन से दो प्राथमिक कार्य संभालते हैं?
o: They cleave phosphodiester bonds and digest the nuclear lipid membrane
They provide structural cores for primary DNA coiling and use basic residues to neutralize the acidic DNA backbone (डीएनए को लपेटना एवं अम्लीय आवेश को उदासीन करना)
They polymerize free deoxynucleotides into long linear polyolefins
They isolate nitrogenous bases to block all central dogma pathways
e: Explanation: Histone octamers act as structural spools that wrap approximately 200 base pairs of DNA to form nucleosomes. Furthermore, their basic residues (lysine and arginine) carry positive charges that neutralize the negative electrical charge of the DNA phosphate backbone.

qe: How do heterochromatin domains contrast fundamentally with euchromatin regions regarding packing density and gene expression states?
qh: पैकिंग घनत्व और जीन अभिव्यक्ति के संबंध में हेटेरोक्रोमैटिन (heterochromatin) और यूक्रोमैटिन (euchromatin) में क्या मुख्य अंतर है?
o: Heterochromatin is loosely packed and highly active transcriptionally
Heterochromatin is densely packed, stains darkly, and is transcriptionally inactive, while euchromatin is loosely coiled and active (हेटेरोक्रोमैटिन का संघनित एवं निष्क्रिय होना)
Heterochromatin lacks core histone octamers entirely across its domains
Both maintain identical highly unstable configurations driven by temperature
e: Explanation: Heterochromatin consists of tightly packed, highly condensed chromatin fibers that stain darkly and are transcriptionally inactive. Euchromatin is loosely packed, allowing transcription machinery to access the DNA to synthesize mRNA.

qe: How does the primary catalytic engine, DNA polymerase III, ensure zero-defect replication along a newly synthesized bacterial DNA strand?
qh: बैक्टीरिया में प्रतिकृति के दौरान, मुख्य एंजाइम डीएनए पॉलीमरेज III (DNA polymerase III) नए बने धागे में त्रुटियों को कैसे ठीक करता है?
o: It dissolves all adjacent carbohydrate rings into single volatile bases
It possesses an intrinsic 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading capability that identifies and removes mismatched bases (प्रूफरीडिंग क्षमता द्वारा गलत क्षारकों को हटाना)
It converts mismatch positions into stable three-dimensional cross-linked resins
It relies on free-radical addition kinetics that ignore steric mismatches
e: Explanation: DNA polymerase III has a built-in proofreading mechanism. If an incorrect nucleotide is added during replication, its 3' to 5' exonuclease activity detects the mismatch, removes the incorrect base, and replaces it with the correct complementary nucleotide.

qe: What parameter structural constraint causes the synthesis of DNA to proceed in a discontinuous fashion (forming Okazaki fragments) along one of the parent template strands?
qh: डीएनए प्रतिकृति के समय एक पैरेंटल धागे पर डीएनए का संश्लेषण असतत (discontinuous) क्यों होता है?
o: The template strand undergoes rapid hydrolytic cleavage under vacuum
DNA-dependent DNA polymerases can catalyze chain elongation exclusively in the 5' to 3' direction along anti-parallel templates (पॉलीमरेज की केवल 5' से 3' दिशा में कार्य करने की क्षमता)
The lagging strand completely lacks ionizable phosphate backbones
The replication loop converts adjacent nucleotides into non-polar gases
e: Explanation: DNA polymerase can synthesize new strands only in the 5' to 3' direction by appending nucleotides to a free 3'-OH group. Because the parent strands are anti-parallel, one strand opens in a direction that forces the polymerase to work backward in short, discontinuous bursts (Okazaki fragments).

qe: If a transcription unit template reads $3'\text{-AATGCAGCTATTAGG-}5'$, what are the exact sequences generated for its complementary DNA strand and its mRNA transcript respectively?
qh: यदि डीएनए के कोडिंग/टेम्पलेट धागे का अनुक्रम $3'\text{-AATGCAGCTATTAGG-}5'$ है, तो इसके पूरक धागे और mRNA का अनुक्रम क्रमशः क्या होगा?
o: Complementary: $5'\text{-TTACGTCGATAATCC-}3'$; mRNA: $5'\text{-UUACGUCGAUAAUCC-}3'$
Complementary: $5'\text{-TTACGTCGATAATCC-}3'$; mRNA: $5'\text{-CGAUUAUCGACGUAA-}3'$ (पूरक और mRNA अनुक्रम)
Complementary: $5'\text{-CGAUUAUCGACGUAA-}3'$; mRNA: $5'\text{-TTACGTCGATAATCC-}3'$
Complementary: $5'\text{-UUACGUCGAUAAUCC-}3'$; mRNA: $5'\text{-CGAUUAUCGACGUAA-}3'$
e: Explanation: Complementary DNA base-pairing rules yield 5'-TTACGTCGATAATCC-3'. When transcribing the template into RNA, uracil (U) replaces thymine (T), resulting in an mRNA sequence of 5'-CGAUUAUCGACGUAA-3' when oriented properly relative to the transcription orientation.

qe: What architectural molecular feature defines the genomic property known as DNA polymorphism encountered across human tracking profiles?
qh: मानव जीनोम मैपिंग में प्रयुक्त डीएनए बहुरूपता (DNA polymorphism) का मुख्य कारण क्या है?
o: The continuous free-radical addition polymerization of cross-linked sugars
Heritable variations and mutations arising within non-coding nucleotide sequences across a population (गैर-कोडिंग अनुक्रमों में वंशागत उत्परिवर्तन)
The complete conversion of purine loops into volatile open-chain amides
The complete lack of asymmetric chiral configurations along macro backbones
e: Explanation: DNA polymorphism refers to variations in the DNA sequence caused by mutations that occur in non-coding regions of the genome.
